de27_origins.topic: Palantir founding, control structure, products, Karp

claims.text: Palantir founded 2003 by Peter Thiel with Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale, Alex Karp and Nathan Gettings; Karp hired as CEO 2004; In-Q-Tel invested about $2 million when Palantir launched in 2004 (other accounts give 2005)

Gotham released 2008; AIP launched April 2023; HQ moved to Denver August 2020; direct public offering on NYSE 30 September 2020; added to S&P 500 (announced 6 Sept 2024); listing moved to Nasdaq effective 26 Nov 2024; Feb 2026 announced move to Miami

10-Q Q2 2026: Class A 1 vote/share (2,300,517 thousand outstanding), Class B 10 votes/share (101,375 thousand), Class F 1,005 thousand shares held in a voting trust 'established by Stephen Cohen, Alexander Karp, and Peter Thiel'; gives Founders ability to control 'up to 49.999999% of the total voting power', conditional on holding at least 100 million equity securities as of 30 June 2026
10-Q Q2 2026: no customer exceeded 10% of total revenue; Q2 2026 revenue $1,935,464 thousand vs $1,003,697 thousand Q2 2025
Karp's Frankfurt doctorate (Aggression in der Lebenswelt, on Parsons) was supervised by Karola Brede, not Habermas; Habermas asked Brede to meet him; Karp drew on Habermas's Lebenswelt concept

de27_capability.topic: What Palantir software does; company's own account; Karp quotes; LAPD study

claims.text: Palantir: 'We do not collect, store, or sell personal data'; 'we act as a data processor, not a data controller'; customers 'define what can and cannot be done with their data'; 'We do not and cannot reuse or transfer our clients' data for our own purposes'
Palantir: default configuration makes user actions traceable (audit logging); fine-grained access controls; 'technical controls alone cannot avert negative societal outcomes'

Karp to Axios on HBO (May 2020): product used 'on occasion' to target and kill; 'you're probably doing the operation that actually takes out the person with another product we built'; on ICE contract regrets: 'No, no, no'; 'I've had some of my favorite employees leave ... over ICE'
Karp on investor call (clip posted 3 Feb 2025): Palantir is here to disrupt institutions and, when necessary, 'to scare enemies and on occasion kill them'

Brayne (ASR Oct 2017; 75 LAPD officers/staff interviewed): LAPD Palantir system includes people never in direct contact with police, linked to persons of interest (e.g., in a car accident with a gang member; a 'lover' relation category); ALPR reads feed system; risk point system feedback loop; Palantir worked with LAPD since 2011; Palantir and LAPD declined comment

The Technological Republic by Alexander C. Karp and Nicholas W. Zamiska (Palantir's head of corporate affairs), Crown Currency, 18 February 2025; offers a critique of 'Silicon Valley's failure to come to the defense of the nation that made its rise possible'

Palantir posted 22-point summary of the book on X, 18 April 2026: 'National service should be a universal duty'; 'Silicon Valley owes a moral debt to the country that made its rise possible'; question is who builds AI weapons, not whether

de27_europe.topic: Swiss, German, UK NHS, Danish decisions on Palantir

claims.text: Zurich Commercial Court, ruling of 4 June 2026 (public 12 June): Republik prevailed on 22 of 23 counter-statements Palantir demanded; one minor correction on a product's development history
Palantir accepted the ruling and will not appeal (SRF, 29 June 2026); Republik's Fichter: Palantir tried for seven years to win Swiss authorities and was rebuffed

Republik/WAV (Dec 2025): 59 requests to 41 federal offices; at least nine approaches by Palantir over seven years; ~20-page Swiss army report advised against, citing risk that data could flow to US government agencies, dependence, sovereignty; Palantir: 'not a surveillance company', no data passed to US authorities, would resist such orders

BVerfG 16 Feb 2023: Hesse §25a(1) HSOG and Hamburg §49(1) HmbPolDVG unconstitutional; automated data analysis needs a 'sufficiently identifiable danger' threshold; Hesse provision continues with restrictions until 30 Sept 2023; Hamburg void; hessenDATA named, Palantir not
Reuters: Hesse used the system since 2017; Palantir's Jan Hiesserich: company 'merely provides the software for processing data, not the data itself'

Baden-Württemberg parliament voted 113-22 (Nov 2025) to let police use Palantir Gotham from Q2 2026, with resolution for a European alternative by 2030; Bavaria (VeRA), NRW, Hesse use Palantir; GFF suits pending
Germany ruled out Palantir's Maven Smart System for the Bundeswehr in April 2026; Bundeswehr evaluating 30 AI tools, mostly German; prototype Q2 2027, deployment 2028 (Vice Adm. Thomas Daum, Reuters)

UK: Liz Kendall said (June 2026) government reviewing £330m NHS FDP contract (awarded 2023), initial term ends early 2027; cited patient confidentiality, public trust, reliance on US supplier; Sadiq Khan blocked £50m Met police contract in May 2026
NISTA raised FDP whole-life cost to £1.1bn, benefits cut to £808m; still green rating; two Commons committees urged break clause; NHS England apologised in August for DPIA error
Louis Mosley: review clause 'good and normal practice'; warned of 'ideologically motivated campaigners'
Danish Justice Ministry answer (10 May 2021) describes POL-INTEL as integrating internal and external data sources but names no vendor
Wikipedia: Danish POL-INTEL operational since 2017, based on Gotham; NHS FDP £330m seven years, Nov 2023
